subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: Should arbitrary executable plugin sources fail closed without acknowledgement while ClawHub, bundled metadata, and official-catalog mappings bypass the warning, with `--force` serving as both acknowledgement and overwrite authorization?
rationale: This deliberately changes a shipped CLI and automation contract while defining which executable sources OpenClaw treats as trusted, so implementation correctness cannot substitute for owner intent.

options.title: Approve the proposed boundary
options.body: Adopt the centralized taxonomy and dual-purpose `--force` contract after an exact-head refresh and required Codex-source check.

options.title: Separate acknowledgement from overwrite
options.body: Keep the centralized taxonomy but introduce a dedicated provenance acknowledgement flag so `--force` retains its existing replacement meaning.

options.title: Defer fail-closed enforcement
options.body: Limit the change to warnings until maintainers choose a permanent cross-surface trust and noninteractive-install contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the proposed boundary
recommendation.body: Adopt the centralized taxonomy and dual-purpose `--force` contract after an exact-head refresh and required Codex-source check.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history most strongly connects this person to plugin installation security, lifecycle, and review decisions.
